focus: A2 loader ground truth and real v2 types: what the real @opencode/plugin 2.0.32 types declare, and which plugin default-export shapes v1 1.19.3 and v2 load

graphEvents.label: Which plugin shape loads and behaves correctly on both v1 and v2
Does 2.0.32 match the 1.18.34 preview and what is the real context domain list
Real 2.0.32 context type is Context with 26 members; PluginContext does not exist
Dual shape is a plain object carrying both setup and server; no two-file split

label: The real 2.0.32 API names the plugin context type Context with 26 members (app, location, options, agent, aisdk, command, credential, event, experimental, integration, mcp, model, generate, permission, plugin, provider, reference, rpc, session, shell, skill, storage, tool, vcs, websearch, worktree); grep for PluginContext across dist/promise/*.d.ts returns zero hits, so any code importing PluginContext from @opencode/plugin fails to compile.

The 1.18.34 preview is not a subset of 2.0.32: it declares a catalog domain (AgentHooks-style CatalogHooks & Reload) that does not exist in the shipping 2.0.32 Context, while 18 real domains (app, location, credential, event, experimental, mcp, model, generate, permission, provider, rpc, session, shell, storage, tool, vcs, websearch, worktree) are absent from the preview; the preview's .plugin domain is also wider than 2.0.32's Pick<PluginApi,"list">.

Real 2.0.32 setup returns Cleanup | void (Cleanup = () => Promise<void> | void) and the compiled adapter honours it via Effect.acquireRelease, while the preview declared setup returning void only; this confirms iteration 1's UNVERIFIED row mapping v1 Hooks.dispose to a v2 cleanup returned from setup, and shows define() is an identity function so a plain object literal is equivalent.

OpenCode v1 1.19.3 accepts all three probed default-export shapes but dispatches them differently: a plain async function is invoked with the full 7-key PluginInput (client, project, worktree, directory, experimental_workspace, serverUrl, $); an object { id, setup, server } has server() invoked and setup NOT invoked; a function carrying .id and .setup is called as an ordinary function with those properties ignored. Module evaluation is unordered (01, 02, 00).

The dual-compatible plugin shape is the plain object { id, setup, server }: v2 runs the setup leg (adapter calls plugin.setup unconditionally and rejects bare and hybrid functions) and v1 runs the server leg, so a two-file split is NOT mandatory; the object must however be written without a strict Plugin annotation because server is not a declared key and excess-property checking would reject the literal.

opencode debug config is a v1 command that loads plugins with no model call, while opencode debug startup does not load plugins at all (it printed only a timing number and wrote no markers); opencode debug --help enumerates config, lsp, rg, file, scrap, skill, snapshot, startup, agent, v2, info, paths and wait as the probe surface.

v1 .opencode/plugins/ discovery is anchored at the invocation cwd, not the git worktree root: a probe project nested several levels below the repo root had its own .opencode/plugins loaded, while config resolution did ascend to the repo root (debug config printed the root mcp.code_mode, permission and agent blocks); whether ancestor plugin directories are additionally unioned stays unverified because the repo plugins emit no load-time marker.

@opencode/plugin 2.0.32 is ESM-only with no require condition on any exports subpath, five sibling @opencode/* dependencies pinned to exactly 2.0.32, @ai-sdk/provider 3.0.8 and effect 4.0.1, and optional peer deps on @opentui/core, @opentui/solid, solid-js and @opencode/theme; a CJS-loaded dual plugin cannot import from it at runtime and exact-pinned sibling packages risk colliding with a v1 dependency tree.

v1-only PluginInput capabilities have no direct 2.0.32 analogue: runtime observation confirms v1 supplies $ (BunShell), serverUrl and experimental_workspace, none of which appear on the real 2.0.32 Context (which offers location, app and shell instead); any of the 16 repo plugins shelling out through PluginInput.$ therefore needs a ctx.shell rewrite rather than a mapping.

A plugin module intended to load on both hosts MUST default-export a non-callable object with a callable id, a callable setup and a callable server; it must not default-export a function and must not rely on a Plugin type annotation, because annotations with excess-property checking reject the server key and a function export is rejected by v2.

v2 plugin code must be type-checked against the real @opencode/plugin 2.0.32 package (or its packed tarball), never against the dist/v2 preview bundled in @opencode-ai/plugin 1.18.34, because that preview names the type PluginContext, declares a removed catalog domain and omits 18 shipping domains.

The setup leg (v2) and the server leg (v1) of a dual plugin share only the options surface; PluginInput and Context have no common domain beyond options, so each leg must build its own runtime and cannot be a single parameterised bootstrap.

direction: Two separate plugin files (one v1 factory module, one v2 object module) as the mandatory dual-support mechanism
reason: v1 1.19.3 accepts the plain { id, setup, server } object and invokes its server method, so one module serves both hosts; a two-file split adds a synchronisation burden no loader requires.

direction: Type-checking v2 work against .opencode/node_modules/@opencode-ai/plugin/dist/v2 as the compatibility target
reason: The preview is wrong in both directions versus 2.0.32: it declares a catalog domain that was removed and omits 18 domains that ship, so it cannot validate real v2 code.

direction: Using opencode debug startup as the v1 plugin-load probe
reason: Empirically wrote no markers while debug config wrote all three, so startup prints timing without instantiating the plugin loader.
